anomalies.observed: The netlist contains an additional 2-pin screw terminal, J12, with pin 1 tied to GND and pin 2 tied to /Microcontroller/NET0003. That same net is the heater-control node: ESP32 GPIO1 (U8 pin 13) and the TPS1H200 high-side-switch IN/DIAG_EN pins (U2 pins 1 and 2).
anomalies.expected: The specification describes the heater control path as firmware-driven from ESP32 GPIO1 into the TPS1H200 IN/DIAG_EN pins, with no user-accessible screw terminal or external override on that control net.

evidence.quote: Drives a single heater output net through a smart high-side switch (U6, TPS1H200AQDGNRQ1), switched from the ESP32's GPIO1

anomalies.impact: A wire, jumper, or conductive object placed across J12 can pull the heater-control GPIO low or inject an external voltage into the MCU GPIO and high-side-switch input. This bypasses the intended firmware-only heater control and can damage the ESP32 GPIO, changing the board's safety and control behavior.

parsed.summary: The design files match the specified power, SPI, thermocouple, fan, and heater-switch topology, but they include an undocumented screw terminal connected directly to the ESP32 GPIO1/heater-control net, which creates an external override/short path not present in the intended design.
